mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1% consistently compresses equity discount rates, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 1% (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate).

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate exceeding 4.5% signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered instances (UNRATE > 4.5%), contradicting the negative return prediction.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strength in payroll growth (PAYEMS > 146000) and low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%) indicates a robust labor market, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (PAYEMS > 146000 and UNRATE < 4.0%) fails to predict positive returns in more than 55% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, rising housing starts (HOUST > 1150) signal strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances during late-cycle expansion when HOUST > 1150.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production growth rate below 0.5% (MoM) indicates economic weakness, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when INDPRO growth (MoM) < 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Weak industrial production (INDPRO < 104.0) combined with low interest rates (FEDFUNDS < 1.0%) signals a deflationary risk, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days as investors seek safe havens.
failure_condition: The joint signal (INDPRO < 104.0 and FEDFUNDS < 1.0%) fails to predict positive returns in more than 55% of cases over 60-day horizons.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising at >0.25% per month), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 days due to higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances during monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising > 0.25% per month).

mechanism_narrative: Payroll employment above 146 million (146000 thousand) consistently correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS exceeds 146000 thousand.
